A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GAS, with matching research objectives, architecture, experiments, and Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative synthesis experiments, component ablations, runtime measurements, and input-view robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative and qualitative comparisons of outputs before and after video diffusion.

M1.justification: The generalizable human NeRF, SMPL geometry cue, appearance conditioning, video diffusion model, and task switcher remain unchanged. Sections 3 and Appendix C retain the same objectives, training procedure, and inference guidance.

E1.justification: Both versions use THuman2.1, 2K2K, MVHumanNet, TikTok, and additional internet videos for the same view and pose synthesis tasks. Revised real-world illustrations remain within the existing evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Animate Anyone and Champ remain the benchmark comparators. v2 additionally quantifies raw generalizable-NeRF output as a component baseline against the complete pipeline in Table 4 and Figure 12; v1 showed intermediate NeRF output qualitatively.

E3.justification: v2 adds a before/after-diffusion control comparison for both synthesis tasks. Existing dataset splits, metrics, training budgets, baseline fine-tuning, and benchmark testing procedures remain unchanged. The new ablation does not clearly identify its quantitative evaluation datasets.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix D.6 add an ablation testing the diffusion stage's contribution, with quantitative results and a qualitative MVHumanNet example. Other ablations are retained; v2 Table 3 reproduces the full cue ablation already present in v1 Appendix Table 10.

E5.justification: Table 11 retains the same means and standard deviations across input-view directions. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports before/after-diffusion FVD values of 517.7/191.3 for novel views and 1255.8/362.0 for poses, alongside other metrics. Tables 1–2 and matched earlier appendix tables retain their values. Several qualitative result panels are revised or expanded.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the reconstruction losses, and mathematical model definitions retain their substance. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The substantive claims remain unified single-image view/pose synthesis, dense conditioning, disentangled synthesis, and improved generalization. Although v2 removes the switcher from the standalone contribution bullets, its claimed function remains in the introduction, method, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix D.6 adds an interpretation distinguishing NeRF's identity preservation near observed views from diffusion's refinement of distant views. Appendix A specifies fine-detail degradation and suggests higher resolution. Appendix E.2 removes tentative explanations for camera-trajectory failures while retaining the failure observation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, training time, and inference runtime information are retained in Section 4.1.2 and the appendices. The project URL is relocated, and dataset-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including TeCH, Pippo, PSHuman, and SIGMAN, and expands discussion of non-rigid animation versus skinning and postprocessing. HumanSplat and MimicMotion are removed from the bibliography. The overall positioning remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, portions of related work, method explanations, experimental discussion, and conclusion. It also reorganizes Appendix D, shortens the contribution list, and adds acknowledgements, constituting broad editorial revision.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and moved onto the first page; Figures 3 and 7 are revised. The full appendix cue-ablation table replaces the abbreviated main-text table, Table 4 and Figure 12 are added, and multiple displays are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new diffusion-stage ablation provides useful direct evidence for a central component, while the fuller main-text cue ablation and revised illustrations improve access to supporting results. The gain is limited: benchmark coverage, existing scores, and reproducibility information are unchanged, and the new quantitative ablation's datasets are not clearly labeled.
